passage: Dear diary, Seema here, and I'm in a weird mood. Today at break I called Jomon a baby, again, because he wouldn't skip games period to sit on the terrace with us. "Rule follower," I said, and Ria laughed. He went red and walked off to the ground alone. I felt clever for about a minute. Now, sitting here, I keep thinking about how hard I pushed. Why did I need him to come so badly? I think if he had joined, I'd feel less silly for doing it. I do get nervous when someone calmly says no, because it makes me look at my own choice. Tomorrow I might just say sorry, and not drag anyone along. Anyone can pick their own way. 😅

qa.q: What did Seema call Jomon at break?
qa.a: Seema called him a baby and a rule follower.

qa.q: Why did Seema push Jomon so hard to join, and what does Seema realise?
qa.a: Seema realises the push came from wanting Jomon to join so Seema would feel less silly about the choice, and that a calm no brings nerves and forces a look at that choice.

qa.q: What could Seema do the next day?
qa.a: Say sorry to Jomon, accept that he can choose differently, and stop dragging others into Seema's own plans.

qa.q: How might Jomon have felt when Seema called him a baby?
qa.a: Embarrassed and hurt. He went red and walked off alone, though he still kept his choice.

grounding: Seema looks down on a rule-following friend, then sees the insecurity behind it and resolves to respect different choices.

passage:
So, Preeti, you asked me why I changed. I'm Jatin, and here's the honest version.
In Class 9, I was the guy who did everything first. Bunking class, sneaking into the late movie, riding without a helmet. Anyone who said no, I called a baby. I said it to you too, remember? When you wouldn't bunk science.
I thought I was braver than everyone. Then one night, I got caught by my uncle, riding his scooter without a licence. He didn't shout. He asked, "Who are you trying to impress?"
That stuck. I realised I was terrified of looking weak. Calling others babies made me feel less scared. It was the same insecurity I mocked in them.
Now, if someone says no, I just say, "Cool." And when you went to science that day, you were the brave one.

qa.q: What did Jatin's uncle catch him doing?
qa.a: Riding his uncle's scooter without a licence.

qa.q: What was Jatin really feeling when he called others babies?
qa.a: He was insecure and terrified of looking weak, and mocking others made him feel less scared.

qa.q: What does Jatin do differently now, and why is it better?
qa.a: He simply says 'Cool' when someone says no, respecting different choices instead of pushing them into his risks.

qa.q: How might Preeti have felt when Jatin called her a baby for not bunking science?
qa.a: Preeti probably felt hurt and pressured, even though choosing to go to class took real courage.

grounding: A teen who called rule-following friends babies sees the same insecurity in himself and starts respecting their choices.

passage:
Monday. Simran rolled her eyes when Minakshi said she wouldn't sneak out of the school fair to go to the mall. "Such a baby. Your mummy will cry, na?" The others laughed. Minakshi went red and stayed back.
Wednesday. Simran lay awake remembering something. At her old school, the older girls had called her "baby" for not trying their cigarettes, and she'd hated it. She'd sworn she'd never be the scared one again. Now she was the one saying it.
Saturday. At the next outing, Simran didn't push. When Minakshi said she'd stay at the book stall, Simran shrugged. "Fine, meet you there after." Later she even walked over and flipped through a book beside her.
Minakshi glanced at her, surprised. "No 'baby' today?"
Simran shook her head. "You were right to do your thing. I was being stupid."

qa.q: Where did Minakshi refuse to sneak off to?
What did Simran realise on Wednesday night?
qa.a: She felt uneasy and ashamed, realising she was mocking Minakshi the same way she had been mocked, out of her own insecurity.

qa.q: What changed in Simran's behaviour on Saturday, and why does it matter?
qa.a: She stopped pushing and respected Minakshi's choice, even joining her at the book stall, instead of forcing her into risks.

qa.q: How does Minakshi react to Simran's change?
qa.a: Minakshi is surprised and a little wary, asking whether there will be no 'baby' today.

grounding: A teen who mocks a rule-following friend sees her own insecurity and learns to respect different choices.
